transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, yeah… I guess what brings me in is work stuff, mostly. I work in meat processing, and there are all these sanitation steps and batch logs and end-of-line paperwork, and I’ll start them—I know how to do them—but then somehow I leave out the last parts.

And it’s not like I don’t care. I know my job depends on finishing them correctly. It’s just… I get through most of it and then it’s like my brain has already moved on. Like yesterday I was thinking about whether I’d taken chicken out of my freezer at home, which isn’t even relevant, and then later I realized I hadn’t finished the paperwork. It’s been happening enough that I’m worried.
Does this happen to you in other areas of your life, outside of work?

Yeah, I mean… outside work, probably, but the thing I’m most worried about is at work because it’s so obvious there. Like I’ll start the sanitation steps or the batch log, and I really do know the order—I’ve done it enough times—and then I’ll get almost to the end and somehow just not finish the last parts.

It’s frustrating because it’s not like I’m trying to skip it. I know it matters, and I know my job depends on it being complete. But my brain kind of… wanders off before the task is actually done.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with friends or family because of this issue with not finishing tasks?

Um… relationships? I don’t know. I mean, not that I’ve really noticed in a big way. My family will get annoyed if I say I’ll do something and then don’t get around to finishing it, but I’m not sure if that’s the same thing you mean.

Like, my mom will remind me about stuff and then I’ll be like, “Yeah, I know,” and then somehow we’re talking about groceries or whether the dog ate something weird, and I’ve completely lost track of the original thing. But I wouldn’t say it’s caused, like, major relationship problems. Or… I don’t think so.
Do you feel like this issue with not finishing tasks is affecting your overall quality of life?

Yeah… yeah, I think it is. I mean, I try not to be dramatic about it, because everybody messes up paperwork sometimes, but it’s gotten to where I’ve had formal retraining meetings at work. Like sitting down and going over the steps again, even though I already know them, which feels awful.

And then my coworkers end up covering parts of what I was supposed to finish, and I hate that because I don’t want to be that person on the line. I want to be reliable. I keep thinking about being moved off the line or fired, and then I go home and I’m still thinking about it while I’m trying to make dinner or whatever.

So yeah, it’s affecting me. It makes me feel like I’m becoming a safety concern instead of someone people can count on.
Do you often feel anxious or worried about making mistakes at work?

Yeah, definitely. I worry about it a lot—probably more than I let on at work. Because it’s not just like, “Oh, I forgot a small thing,” it turns into meetings where they retrain me on stuff I already know, and then I feel embarrassed sitting there like I’m brand new.

And then if I miss finishing something, someone else has to cover part of my job, and I hate that. I don’t want coworkers thinking they have to babysit me or double-check everything I touch. I start thinking, like, what if they move me off the line, or what if this is the thing that gets me fired?

It’s weird because I’ll be doing something totally normal later, like making food at home, and I’m still replaying whether I messed up at work. I just keep feeling like I’m becoming a safety concern instead of someone they can trust.
Do you often find yourself forgetting things that just happened?

Yeah… kind of. Like, especially when someone tells me something out loud. My supervisor will give me directions face-to-face, and I’ll be standing there nodding like, okay, yes, I’m getting this.

And then like a minute later, I realize I only really held onto the first part. The rest is just… gone, or fuzzy. Then I have to ask someone else, “Wait, what did she say after that?” which is embarrassing because I was literally right there.

It’s not like I’m trying not to listen. I’ll think I am listening, and then my brain just keeps one piece and drops the rest.
Do you feel like your difficulty finishing tasks or remembering instructions affects how you interact with friends or family?

I mean… with friends or family, I guess it comes out mostly because I’m already stressed from work. Like, the big thing is work, honestly. That’s where it’s actually caused problems—formal retraining meetings and coworkers having to finish or cover pieces of what I was supposed to do.

And then I bring that home in my head, so if someone in my family asks me something, I might be kind of distracted because I’m thinking, “Am I going to get moved off the line? Are they going to fire me?” It makes me feel ashamed, like I’m not dependable.

Sorry, I know you asked about friends and family. I just keep coming back to work because that’s where it feels the worst. I feel like I’m becoming a safety concern instead of the reliable person I want to be.
Do you ever avoid starting tasks at work because you're worried about not being able to finish them?

Yeah… I do. Not every single task, but the ones where I know it’s going to be a lot of reading or rules, I’ll avoid starting them. Like the certification modules at work—I put those off until the absolute last minute.

And any long procedure reading, too. I know it’s important, especially with safety stuff, but sitting there trying to actually absorb all of it feels… I don’t know, almost physically exhausting. Like I’ll open it and then suddenly I’m thinking I should clean my locker or check something else first, which is ridiculous because it doesn’t make the module go away.

So yeah, I avoid starting those because I’m worried I’m not going to get through it or actually retain it.
Have you noticed any problems in your personal relationships or daily life outside of work that you think might be related to your difficulty finishing tasks or remembering things?

Um… outside of work, I think it mostly shows up because work is so bad right now. Like I’ll be at home but still thinking about what happened on the line, or whether people had to cover for me again.

I know you asked about personal relationships and daily life, but honestly the biggest impact is at work. I’ve had formal retraining meetings, and coworkers have had to take over parts of what I was supposed to do. And then I go home feeling like… I don’t know, like I’m becoming a safety problem instead of someone people can count on.

So maybe it affects home because I’m carrying that fear around—like, am I going to get moved off the line, or fired? It makes me kind of ashamed and distracted around people.
Have you lost any friends because of your difficulty finishing tasks or remembering things?

I don’t think I’ve, like… lost a friend outright because of it. Not that I know of.

I mean, I worry people get annoyed with me, and then I start thinking about whether I forgot to text someone back or follow through on something, but I can’t point to someone and say, “Yeah, they stopped being my friend because of that.” Most of my brain goes to work stuff lately, honestly, so I might not even be tracking that clearly.
Do you feel like your difficulties at work have affected your relationships with friends or family in a significant way?

I’m not really sure it’s been significant with friends or family. Like, I don’t think anyone has sat me down and said, “You’re being distant,” or anything like that.

I mean, sometimes I’m quieter after work, and then my family will ask if I’m okay, but then I’m thinking about the whole day and whether I messed something up, and also there’s always just normal life stuff—like laundry or dinner or whatever—so it’s hard to separate.

So… maybe a little, in the sense that I’m distracted or stressed, but I don’t know if I’d say it’s really affected the relationships themselves in a big way.
Do you often feel sad or depressed?

I don’t know if I’d call it depressed exactly. Like, I get upset and kind of down about how things are going, especially after a bad shift, but then I start thinking about, like, did I label something wrong, did someone have to fix it, and then it turns into this whole spiral about work.

So… sad sometimes, yeah, but I’m not sure if that’s the same as being depressed. I guess I’m not totally sure what you mean by often.
Do you feel sad or empty most of the day?

Um… most of the day? I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I feel empty, exactly. Sad comes and goes, I guess, but it’s not like I wake up and the whole day is just… that.

Sometimes I’ll feel kind of low, especially if something at work is hanging over me, and then I’ll get distracted by, like, what I need to do when I get home or whether I remembered to take something out of the freezer—sorry, that’s random—but yeah, I don’t think I feel sad or empty most of the day. At least I haven’t really noticed it that way.
Do you think your difficulties with finishing tasks and remembering things are significantly interfering with your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

Yeah… I think at work it is, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it’s gotten to the point where I’ve had formal retraining meetings about stuff I should already know, and coworkers end up covering parts of what I’m supposed to be doing.

And then I start worrying, like, are they going to move me off the line, or fire me? Which is embarrassing to even say. I want to be reliable, you know? But sometimes it feels like I’m becoming more of a safety concern than someone they can count on.

Daily life is… I don’t know, that’s harder to measure, because everyone forgets laundry or loses track of errands sometimes. But at work, yeah, it’s definitely interfering.
Do you think you would be able to finish tasks if you had someone reminding you or helping you stay on track?

Maybe? Like, if someone was right there reminding me, I think I’d do better, but that’s also kind of the problem. I’ll start the sanitation steps or the batch logs, and I know what the ending is supposed to be, but then somehow I leave out the last part.

It’s stupid because it’s not like I don’t understand the job. I can be doing the end-of-line paperwork and then I think, okay, I need to check one more thing, and then someone asks me something or I notice a tray is out of place, and suddenly I’ve walked away like it’s finished when it isn’t.

So yeah, reminders would probably help, but I hate that I’d need that much watching just to finish things that I know matter. My job kind of depends on doing those last pieces correctly.
Do you think your worries about work are causing you to have trouble finishing tasks, or do you think there's something else going on that's making it hard for you to focus?

I think the worrying makes it worse, probably, because then I’m thinking about whether I’m messing up, which is its own whole loop. But it doesn’t feel like that’s the only reason.

Even when I come in for a shift telling myself, like, okay, today I’m going to really stay locked in, after a while the cutting and weighing and checking labels just sort of… blur together. And then I’ll realize I’ve been staring at the same tray or the same log sheet, but I’m not actually taking in what I’m supposed to do next.

It’s weird because I’m there, I’m looking at it, but my brain isn’t staying with it. And then I’ll snap back and be like, wait, did I already do this part, or was I about to do it? So yeah, the worry is there, but I think something else is happening with my focus too.
Do you feel like your difficulties with tasks and memory are causing problems in your personal life outside of work?

I mean… outside of work, it’s harder for me to say clearly. Like, I’ll forget little things at home and then start thinking about whether that counts or if I’m just being messy, and then I end up comparing it to work because that’s where it’s really obvious.

At work it’s not just annoying anymore. I’ve had those formal retraining meetings, and coworkers have had to step in and cover parts of what I was supposed to finish. And that makes me feel awful, because I don’t want people thinking they have to babysit me on the line.

I guess in my personal life it bothers me mostly because I carry that stress home. I keep thinking, what if they move me off the line, or what if I get fired? I feel like I’m starting to look like a safety concern instead of someone reliable, and that’s… yeah, that really gets to me.
Have you felt like your difficulties with tasks and memory have significantly affected your relationships with friends or family?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I can point to, like, a specific friendship ending or my family saying I’m impossible to deal with because of it.

Sometimes I wonder if I’m just more stressed when I’m around them, because I’ll be thinking about work in the background and then I’m not totally present. Like my mom will be talking and I’ll realize I was half listening, but then I don’t know if that’s the same thing you mean.

So… I guess it affects me, but I don’t know if it’s significantly affected the relationships themselves. I haven’t really asked them, I guess.
Do you feel like your difficulties with tasks and memory are significantly impacting your ability to interact with others or perform daily activities outside of work?

I don’t really know how to measure that. Like, outside of work I still do things, I’m not just… completely unable to function or anything. But I do get kind of scattered, and then I start thinking about work again, and then I’m not really paying attention to whoever I’m with.

Like the other day—well, not the other day, but sometimes I’ll be with my roommate or on the phone with my mom, and I’m listening, but then I’m thinking about whether I forgot something on the line or if someone had to fix my mistake, and suddenly I missed half of what they said.

But I don’t know if that’s a daily activity problem exactly. I guess I’m not sure. It feels like work is where it really shows up, and everything else is more like… spillover from being stressed about it.
Do you have difficulty paying attention to details or making careless mistakes in your daily activities outside of work?

I’m not totally sure outside of work. Like, if you mean at home, I don’t have a clear example where I’m like, “yes, I definitely messed that up because I missed a detail.” I probably do little things, but then I start second-guessing whether everyone does that.

At work it’s easier to notice because there are consequences and people see it, but daily life is more… fuzzy. Like if I misplace something or forget part of what I was doing, I don’t always think of it as a careless mistake, I just think, “I’m tired” or “I’m stressed.” So I guess I haven’t really noticed a specific pattern outside of work.

So yeah, reminders would probably help, but I hate that I’d need that much watching just to finish things that I know matter. My job kind of depends on doing those last pieces correctly.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are primarily due to anxiety or another underlying condition
doctor.question: Do you think your worries about work are causing you to have trouble finishing tasks, or do you think there's something else going on that's making it hard for you to focus?

target_item.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: Even when I start a shift trying really hard to stay locked in, after a while the cutting, weighing, and checking labels all blur together and I realize I’ve been staring at the same tray or log sheet without taking in what I’m supposed to do next.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the problem is mainly worry-driven or whether there is an underlying difficulty focusing and sustaining attention during tasks.

patient.answer:
I think the worrying makes it worse, probably, because then I’m thinking about whether I’m messing up, which is its own whole loop. But it doesn’t feel like that’s the only reason.

Even when I come in for a shift telling myself, like, okay, today I’m going to really stay locked in, after a while the cutting and weighing and checking labels just sort of… blur together. And then I’ll realize I’ve been staring at the same tray or the same log sheet, but I’m not actually taking in what I’m supposed to do next.

It’s weird because I’m there, I’m looking at it, but my brain isn’t staying with it. And then I’ll snap back and be like, wait, did I already do this part, or was I about to do it? So yeah, the worry is there, but I think something else is happening with my focus too.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences significant distress or impairment in social or personal life due to their symptoms
doctor.question: Do you feel like your difficulties with tasks and memory are causing problems in your personal life outside of work?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: At work this has led to formal retraining meetings, coworkers covering parts of my duties, and real fear that I’ll be moved off the line or fired. I feel like I’m becoming a safety concern instead of the reliable worker I want to be.
target_item.reason: The question is asking whether the attention and memory difficulties are causing functional problems outside of work, which is directly about impairment in daily functioning.

patient.answer:
I mean… outside of work, it’s harder for me to say clearly. Like, I’ll forget little things at home and then start thinking about whether that counts or if I’m just being messy, and then I end up comparing it to work because that’s where it’s really obvious.

At work it’s not just annoying anymore. I’ve had those formal retraining meetings, and coworkers have had to step in and cover parts of what I was supposed to finish. And that makes me feel awful, because I don’t want people thinking they have to babysit me on the line.

I guess in my personal life it bothers me mostly because I carry that stress home. I keep thinking, what if they move me off the line, or what if I get fired? I feel like I’m starting to look like a safety concern instead of someone reliable, and that’s… yeah, that really gets to me.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences significant distress or impairment in social relationships due to their symptoms
doctor.question: Have you felt like your difficulties with tasks and memory have significantly affected your relationships with friends or family?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about effects on relationships with friends or family, but the provided symptom profile only describes functional impairment at work and does not cover relationship impairment.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I can point to, like, a specific friendship ending or my family saying I’m impossible to deal with because of it.

Sometimes I wonder if I’m just more stressed when I’m around them, because I’ll be thinking about work in the background and then I’m not totally present. Like my mom will be talking and I’ll realize I was half listening, but then I don’t know if that’s the same thing you mean.

So… I guess it affects me, but I don’t know if it’s significantly affected the relationships themselves. I haven’t really asked them, I guess.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences significant distress or impairment in social or occupational areas due to their symptoms
doctor.question: Do you feel like your difficulties with tasks and memory are significantly impacting your ability to interact with others or perform daily activities outside of work?

target_item.reason: The question asks specifically about significant impact on interacting with others or daily activities outside of work, but the provided symptom profile only documents functional impairment at work and does not clearly cover outside-work social or daily functioning.

patient.answer:
I don’t really know how to measure that. Like, outside of work I still do things, I’m not just… completely unable to function or anything. But I do get kind of scattered, and then I start thinking about work again, and then I’m not really paying attention to whoever I’m with.

Like the other day—well, not the other day, but sometimes I’ll be with my roommate or on the phone with my mom, and I’m listening, but then I’m thinking about whether I forgot something on the line or if someone had to fix my mistake, and suddenly I missed half of what they said.

But I don’t know if that’s a daily activity problem exactly. I guess I’m not sure. It feels like work is where it really shows up, and everything else is more like… spillover from being stressed about it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are better explained by a neurocognitive disorder or an attention disorder
doctor.question: Do you have difficulty paying attention to details or making careless mistakes in your daily activities outside of work?

target_item.reason: The question asks specifically about difficulty paying attention to details or making careless mistakes outside of work, but the provided symptom profile does not include a careless-mistakes/detail-attention item.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure outside of work. Like, if you mean at home, I don’t have a clear example where I’m like, “yes, I definitely messed that up because I missed a detail.” I probably do little things, but then I start second-guessing whether everyone does that.

At work it’s easier to notice because there are consequences and people see it, but daily life is more… fuzzy. Like if I misplace something or forget part of what I was doing, I don’t always think of it as a careless mistake, I just think, “I’m tired” or “I’m stressed.” So I guess I haven’t really noticed a specific pattern outside of work.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of difficulty finishing tasks, forgetfulness, and distractibility, particularly in a work setting, are consistent with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), which is characterized by symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity. While the patient also experiences anxiety and stress related to their work performance, the primary symptoms described align more closely with ADHD.
